title: Server Components, Edge Caching & The New React Data Layer

trending.heading: Trending for you
trending.content:
## Why everyone is rewiring their data layer

This week the developer feeds are dominated by one theme: **moving data fetching out of the client**. With React 19 stabilizing Server Components, teams at scale are reporting **30–50% smaller client bundles** by deleting `useEffect` data-loading code.

### The shift in three points

- **Fetch on the server, stream to the client.** Server Components let you `await` directly in the component body — no loading spinners wired through state.
- **Cache at the edge.** Pairing server fetches with edge caching (`revalidate`) turns a 400ms render into a sub-50ms one for repeat visitors.
- **Type-safety end to end.** Because the fetch and the render live in the same file, your `DigestOutput` type flows straight into JSX with zero serialization guesswork.

> Takeaway: if your dashboard still loads its first screen from a client `useEffect`, you are leaving both performance and DX on the table.

### What changed in practice

The pattern that's winning is small: a thin **server data layer** that every route imports, returning fully typed objects. Components stay dumb renderers. This is exactly the shape this portal now uses for its blog and activity data.
